title: Not selling anything, it's completely free to play. Just showing you my RPG
author: DuchessCupcakeGames
selftext: I wrote the lore, mechanics and story Bible/ rules, then generated about 85 maps for this spawling RPG. Claude, Codex and Lovable did the rest. After about a month of clarifying specifics, it's finally in a good place to share. Absolutely free to play. It's so close to me being ready to get a real domain for it, just a few more tests.

comments.author: Worried_Number5115
comments.body:
I really like the map art and character art. 

However, the game is quite clunky imo for a few reasons. 

No walking animations, the player is a static moving image. Text is very chunky and gives a ton to digest at once. Vertical orientation for an RPG makes the screen feel a bit stuffed to me but I get that’s the style and design you went for

replies.author: DuchessCupcakeGames
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback. It's not ideally how I want it. Because I built it completely at the beginning with just a few maps, the text is a little too heavy at the beginning. I meant for it to gradually lead into the story, but bombard the player with too much info right away. I'll spread it out over the 85 maps now that they are built. I never intended to animate the avatars, since it's more of a text based rpg,but that wouldn't be that hard to do. Maybe I'll do that before going totally live. Again, thank you. It's valuable feedback!

replies.author: Camenwolf
replies.body:
I agree with u/Worried_Number5115 .  It's a really gorgeous game, but the lack of animation on the avatar as you move it around the map is jarring.  I know it's more of a text oriented game and the avatar is serving as sort of a map marker.  Still, having it animate would give it that professional touch.

Great concept too, by the way!

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body:
To add to that - it does that thing where coding assistants like to use user-facing surfaces as their own notepad and "justify" their design decisions to the player.

Stuff like "Random attributes — accept your fate. Blocks reroll whole, **never a single number.**" -> "Never a single number" is a self-prompting artifact where the agent reaffirms its prompt in plain user-facing text instead of putting that into a comment where it belongs.

From the same example, there's also a kind of diegetic leakage, where the LLM tries really hard to skew text that is meant to be utility-first and just inform the user into some kind of diegetic message, e.g. "Random attributes — **accept your fate**." -> The "accept your fate" bit is useless information for the user and contributes nothing. It's just the LLM blurring UI and in-game text together.
